item.research_question: What are the deformation and failure mechanisms of an equiatomic CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy subjected to extreme shock loading (strain rates >10^6/s), and how do pre-existing defects influence void nucleation, growth, and coalescence?
item.material_system: Equiatomic CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy (MEA), single-phase face-centered cubic (fcc), cold rolled 80% and annealed at 1000°C for 48 hours (grain size ~100 μm)
item.processing_route: Pulsed laser-driven shock experiments at the Omega laser facility (352-nm wavelength, 1 ns pulse, 100–150 J for VISAR, up to 450 J per beam for spallation); recovery of samples for multiscale characterization (STEM, EBSD, TEM, FIB); Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations using LAMMPS with an embedded atom model potential (single-crystal ~3.84 million atoms, piston-driven shock compression at 5 K, tensile loading at 10^7 s^-1 and 500 K)
item.test_conditions: Strain rates estimated at ~1 × 10^7/s; shock pressures up to 130 GPa (ablation pressure); tensile spall loading upon shock wave release; temperatures estimated to rise locally by a factor of two near voids; strain rates in MD simulations of 10^7 s^-1
key_findings: Spall strength was estimated to be approximately 9.8 GPa at a strain rate of ~1 × 10^7/s.
Shock compression generated a three-dimensional network of planar defects including stacking faults, nanotwins, and hexagonal nanolamella on {111} planes.
Nanoindentation showed a 30% increase in hardness in moderately laser-shocked samples compared to as-received material.
Voids nucleated preferentially in amorphous regions formed at intersections of planar defects and at grain boundaries.
Voids near grain boundaries were generally larger (>20 μm) and more susceptible to coalescence than those in grain interiors.
MD simulations showed that pre-existing nanotwins constrained dislocation glide, changing void geometry from uniform to penny-shaped.
The presence of nanotwins delayed void coalescence, keeping two voids separated under the same applied volumetric strain compared to defect-free samples.
Amorphization occurred in heavily deformed regions where local defect density was sufficiently high, confirmed by reduced radial distribution function peak intensity.
item.mechanism: During shock compression, the low stacking fault energy (SFE) of CrCoNi promotes the homogeneous nucleation of planar defects (stacking faults, twins, hcp lamella) forming a 3D nanointerface network. Upon shock release, tensile stress triggers void nucleation, which occurs preferentially in amorphous regions created by defect intersections and at grain boundaries. During void growth, the pre-existing planar defects constrain the emission and glide of dislocation loops from the void surface, altering void geometry (anisotropic growth) and delaying coalescence, thereby enhancing spall strength and damage tolerance. Thermal softening and shear localization can also occur, leading to nanorecrystallization and amorphization.
item.limitations: The nominal strain rate is not constant due to rapid stress wave decay; systematic experiments at various temperatures and strain rates are needed to quantitatively explore the Zener-Hollomon relationship; the specific effect of amorphization on mechanical behavior is still debated; the results may not be unique to HEAs but also apply to fcc metals with low SFE.
item.future_work: Conduct systematic experiments at various temperatures and strain rates to quantitatively explore the Zener-Hollomon relationship; tailor the SFE of these materials to promote TWIP, TRIP, and amorphization effects to further improve impact resistance; investigate the specific effect of amorphization on mechanical behavior.
quotes: Molecular dynamics simulations corroborate the experimental results and suggest that deformation-induced defects formed before void nucleation govern the geometry of void growth and delay their coalescence.

The pre-existence of planar defects (stacking faults, twins and hexagonal lamella) introduced by shock compression can serve to delay the coalescence of certain voids that generate enhanced spall strength and damage tolerance under dynamic tension conditions.
